questions.q: What does the TIME formula stand for?
a: Treasured, investing, mandatory and empty time
questions.why: Lesson 1 breaks time into treasured, investing, mandatory and empty categories.

questions.q: What is a GIA, according to the summary?
a: A goal you set each quarter
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines the GIA as the greatest-impact activity that serves you most in the long run.

questions.q: What does the summary suggest combining with mandatory time?
a: Learning, like listening to a podcast while commuting
Resting, like napping at your desk
Socializing, like calling friends at work
questions.why: Lesson 1 suggests pairing routine duties with learning, such as a podcast while cooking or commuting.

questions.q: Why tie your goals to a why and a how?
a: It builds motivation and gives concrete steps
It makes goals look impressive to others
It removes the need for priorities
It guarantees you finish on time
questions.why: Lesson 2 says linking goals to a why and a how keeps you motivated and specific about the steps.

questions.q: What should your no be saved for?
questions.why: Lesson 3 says to save refusals for empty time and pointless notifications, not treasured time.
